text:
alex_chen: quick sync — I ran a throughput + latency sweep for the new reranker (v2-rerank-1) across regions/hw. dims: 768 / 1024 / 1536. batch sizes: 1,4,8,16,32,64. hw: A100 40GB, H100 80GB, T4, and a beefy CPU type (c7i/avx512). regions: us-west-2, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1. attaching highlights and a tiny command we used.

bench-bot: auto-report: grafana -> https://grafana.internal/r/rdw/rerank-v2/sweep (private) ; summary: best cost/throughput tradeoff varies a lot with dim & kernel.

maria_garcia: quick note — ap-southeast-1 H100 had higher p99 latency for batch>=32 on 1536 dim, looks like KV cache misses + small kernel fallback. p50 is fine.

alex_chen: exact numbers (rounded vectors/sec for embed/rerank pair inference):
- 768 dim, batch 16: H100 13.2k v/s, A100 9.6k v/s, T4 2.4k v/s, CPU 1.8k v/s
- 1024 dim, batch 16: H100 9.1k, A100 6.8k, T4 1.6k, CPU 1.1k
- 1536 dim, batch 8: H100 5.5k, A100 3.7k, T4 0.85k, CPU 0.6k
Also p99 tail lags: H100 p99 +120ms (ap-southeast-1), A100 +230ms (us-west-2) for 1536/batch32.

kai_patel: interesting. what kernel variants did you run? fused-attn vs split-kernel? quant levels?

alex_chen: we tried two kernel packs: "fused-gemm-attn-v1" (default continuous-batching path) and "split-kernel-conservative" (falls back for long kv/cold). quant: fp16 baseline, int8 dynamic quant (per-channel) for weights in one run. int8 on H100 gave ~1.25x throughput for 1024 dim but p99 regressed ~15-25ms unless we pin batch size <= 16.

samir_rao: CPU details: c7i with AVX512 (x86) + intel-mkl backend. For 768-dim at batch 16 CPU gets ~75% of T4 throughput when using packed GEMM path. But for 1536 dim CPU memory bandwidth kills it. Also the kernel we built for CPU used blocked matmul with streaming loads, helps p50 but p99 still noisy under other tenants.

maria_garcia: localization/regional note: eu-west-1 A100 cluster runs a slightly older kernel build (we forgot a recent optimization). I re-ran on a test node with the new fused-gemm patch — A100 throughput improved ~12% for 1024 dim. Can we schedule an upgrade?

alex_chen: yes please. Kai, can you prod eng-runtime to deploy fused-gemm v0.7 to eu-west-1 dev pool? Put canary at 5% then scale.

kai_patel: will do. quick checklist: run these perf commands on canary nodes: 
```
./perf_runner --model rerank-v2 --dim 1024 --batch 16 --kernel fused-gemm-attn-v0.7 --quant fp16 --iter 1000 --region eu-west-1
```
and for int8: 
```
./perf_runner --model rerank-v2 --dim 1024 --batch 16 --kernel fused-gemm-attn-v0.7 --quant int8-dyn --iter 1000
```
Remember to capture p50/p95/p99 and mem/cold-start counts.

maria_garcia: also flag the KV cache hit ratio metric. On APAC we saw cache misses when requests went to fallback shard (different model variant). That explains p99.

samir_rao: one more datapoint: for embeddings-only (512 dim) throughput delta is smaller — T4 ~6.8k, A100 ~8.9k, H100 ~11.3k at batch 32. So if product can decouple embed vs rerank, cost wins by routing embed-heavy traffic to T4 in eu-west-1 and reserving H100 for reranker heavy flows.

alex_chen: routing policy idea: route by feature_flags + model_variant. cheap-embed -> T4, rerank-large -> H100, fallback -> A100. Need costs modeled.

bench-bot: cost estimate (rough per-hour GPU effective): H100 > A100 ~1.3x ; T4 ~0.25x A100. For the 1024 dim steady traffic with 25% rerank ratio, projected monthly: H100 heavy = $$$ (private link).

kai_patel: action items:
1) eng-runtime: deploy fused-gemm v0.7 to eu-west-1 dev pool (canary 5%). -> @kai_patel
2) eng-ml: re-run int8 vs fp16 p99 sweep with pinned batches {8,16} across all regions. -> @alex_chen @maria_garcia
3) infra: capture KV cache hit rate + fallback counts in apac test. -> @samir_rao
4) cost modeling: route-by-feature proposal and numbers. -> @maria_garcia

alex_chen: thanks everyone. I'll upload CSVs + short figure exports to the grafana link in 30m. If you see >20% p99 regressions on int8, mark rollback. :thumbsup:

maria_garcia: noted. I'll watch apac once canary lands.

bench-bot: deploy scheduled: eu-west-1/dev/fused-gemm-v0.7 canary at 1792349800.
